(Himekawa)|-}} * {{HW}} * {{HWL}} * {{HWDE}} * {{TP (Himekawa)|-}} }} }} ==Characteristics== ==={{OoT|-}}=== {{Descriptions OoT}} Lizalfos brandish swords and have little armor in {{OoT}}. They are very agile, for they are able to jump far out of [[Link]]'s attack range, as well as capable of leaping over the young hero's head to deliver a strike from behind. They first appear in [[Dodongo's Cavern]], where two pairs act as the Dungeons's [[Sub-Boss]]es. Despite having to face off against a duo, Link does not have to fight both simultaneously. One engages the young hero, while the other watches from afar. Befitting their tendency to fight in pairs, after one Lizalfos sustains enough damage, the two switch roles with one another. They are seldom encountered, only appearing as regular enemies later in the [[Spirit Temple]] and in certain other Dungeons in {{MQ}}. A related enemy known as [[Dinolfos]] appear later in the game as well. ==={{TP|-}}=== Lizalfos come in two varieties in {{TP}}. One variety uses an axe blade affixed to their tails, and the second variety makes use of a skull mask. They are easily defeated with [[Bomb Arrow]]s or [[Hidden Skill]]s such as the [[Back Slice]] and the [[Mortal Draw]]. In addition, [[Wolf Link]] is able to leap at and bite at their throats. Lizalfos appear in parts of [[Hyrule Field]] in [[Lanayru Province]] in addition to numerous [[Dungeon]]s, including the [[Lakebed Temple]], the [[Temple of Time]], the [[City in the Sky]], [[Hyrule Castle]], and the [[Cave of Ordeals]]. Dynalfos, similar but much larger and more heavily armored enemies, appear in the Temple of Time and the City in the Sky. They are considerably more dangerous opponents than Lizalfos, capable of dodging the [[Ending Blow]] and blocking many other attacks. A winged variety of Lizalfos called [[Aeralfos]] also appear later in the game.{{Fact}} ==={{SS|-}}=== {{Descriptions SS}} Lizalfos are first encountered in the [[Earth Temple]] as regular enemies in {{SS}}. They later appear as a pair also act as the [[Dungeon]]'s [[Sub-Boss]], guarding the [[Bomb Bag]]. They adorn their forearms with large iron gauntlets that they can utilize in both their offense and defense. For example, the guard prevents them from being knocked over from normal attacks. Besides being adept defenders, Lizalfos are very nimble and can swiftly dodge sword strikes, and they can harm Link by blowing streams of fire and by mashing him with the maces found on the tips of their tails. In addition to the Earth Temple, the saurian creatures can be found at the [[Lanayru Shipyard]], the [[Pirate Stronghold]], and the [[Volcano Summit]]. An efficient way to slay a Lizalfos is to use strong attacks that make them fall on the ground such as the [[Spin Attack]]. After this happens, Link can use the [[Fatal Blow]] to kill them. Defeating a Lizalfos will make it drop a [[Lizard Tail]], which can be collected as [[Treasure]]. A stronger variant known as [[Dark Lizalfos]] appear in the [[Fire Sanctuary]] and [[Sky Keep]]. ==={{BotW|-}}=== {{Compendium/Extract|Lizalfos}} Lizalfos appear as chameleon-like [[Enemy|Enemies]] in {{BotW}}. They will camouflage to their environment and wait for [[Link]] to get near before ambushing him. They are adept swimmers, and can spit globs of [[Water (Terrain)|Water]] at Link to hit him from long range. There are several varieties of Lizalfos, including [[Blue Lizalfos]], [[Black Lizalfos]], [[Silver Lizalfos]], [[Fire-Breath Lizalfos]], [[Ice-Breath Lizalfos]], [[Electric Lizalfos]], and in [[Master Mode]], [[Golden Lizalfos]]. They primarily use [[Weapon]]s of the [[Lizalfos Gear]] equipment archetype, such as [[Lizal Spear]]s that they also use to hunt for [[Fish]]. They are sometimes also encountered utilizing [[Hylian]]-made weapons. When defeated, they may drop [[Lizalfos Horn]]s, [[Lizalfos Talon]]s, and [[Lizalfos Tail]]s. Electric Lizalfos, found in places such as the [[Gerudo Desert]] and [[Zonai Ruins]], have electrified horns that they can use to generate an [[Electricity|Electric]] field. If Link manages to hit said horn with an [[Arrow]], it will cause the Electric Lizalfos to discharge involuntarily. He can use this to his advantage to electrocute nearby Enemies. Ice-Breath Lizalfos, typically found in cold areas, will spit icy projectiles at Link, and are weak to [[Fire]]. Fire-Breath Lizalfos, found in [[Scorching Climate]]s such as [[Death Mountain]] and the Gerudo Desert, can breathe Fire at Link and are vulnerable to [[Ice]]. There are also undead versions of Lizalfos. [[Stalizalfos]] rise from the ground during the night in certain areas and attack Link. [[Cursed Lizalfos]] can sometimes be found spawning from various [[Pool of Malice|Pools of Malice]] throughout Hyrule and within the [[Divine Beast]]s. ====Drops==== {{Collapsible |header= Drops of {{Stub|TotK}} Lizalfos appear as Enemies in {{TotK}}. They resemble their {{BotW}} counterparts, but bear longer, sharper horns, which they can use to attack [[Link]]. Lizalfos are carnivores, and have a diet of [[Meat]], [[Fish]], and small [[Creature]]s such as [[Crab]]s, [[Insect]]s, [[Lizard]]s, and [[Snail]]s. If a Lizalfos that is not in combat spots any of these, it will run to pick it up and eat it. They may either attempt to snatch up their food with their hands or, if that food is a living Creature, catch it with their long tongues. If a Lizalfos is prevented from picking up an edible [[Item]] or catching a Creature, it will stomp the ground and roar in frustration. ==={{EoW|-}}=== {{Checklist |game= EoW |type= Enemies |category= Enemies in Echoes of Wisdom |needs= Detailed information on the following: * The Enemy's behavior * The Enemy's weaknesses * Where the Enemy appears * What the Echo cost is for the Enemy }} {{Stub|EoW}} {{Frameless|[[File:EoW Lizalfos Render 2.png|thumb|right|160px|alt= A render of a dark Lizalfos.|{{Game Label|{{EoW|-}}}}A Still World Lizalfos]]}} {{Descriptions EoW}} Lizalfos appear atop [[Eldin Volcano]] and in the [[Faron Wetlands]], where they wield [[Trident]]s. They are more agile than other [[Monster]]s. If they fall into [[Lava]], they will die. A dark version of Lizalfos appear in the [[Still World]]. Lizalfos will be stunned after they strike a [[Shield]] or a hard [[Object]], such as a [[Boulder]]. ==Other Appearances== ==={{LCT|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} [[File:LCT Temple of Time: Ranger Thumbnail.png|thumb|right|{{Game Label|{{LCT|-}}}}A Lizalfos]] Lizalfos appear as enemies in the [[Temple of Time: Ranger]] [[Stage]] in {{LCT}}. Lizalfos can move quickly and counter Link's attacks. They are able to block [[Link]]'s [[Crossbow]] shots with the gauntlets on their left claws, and attack by slashing either the blades they carry or the blades attached to their tails. They can also jump across the room in an attempt to surround Link. {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{OoT|-}} (Himekawa)=== {{Noncanon|Start}} Lizalfos appear in {{OoT (Himekawa)}}, being summoned by the [[Twinrova]] witches alongside some [[Moblin]]s to try and slow Link down, who shoots an arrow into one's neck. {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{HW|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} [[File:HWDE Lizalfos Mini Map Icon.png|left]] Lizalfos appear as elite enemies in {{HW}}, serving as [[Captain (Hyrule Warriors)|Captains]] in several [[Forces]]. They carry blades and arm gauntlets with them, with which they use to attack and defend with. Lizalfos also hop from side to side in battle. Lizalfos can also attack either by slamming their foes with their tails or by breathing fire in the form of fireballs or streams. When blowing streams of fire, their [[Weak Point Gauge]]s are exposed. They are also weak to [[Bomb]]s. Lizalfos also appear as minor characters in certain [[Scenario]]s. In "[[Ganondorf's Return]]", a Lizalfos leads the [[Monster Forces]] of the [[Gerudo Desert]]. In the Scenario "[[The Dragon of the Caves]]" of [[Cia's Tale]], [[Lizalfos Chieftain]]s appear as Captains in [[Volga's Forces]]. They are accompanied by [[Dinolfos Chieftain]]s, and arrive as reinforcements when [[Cia]] tries to enlist [[Volga]] into her army. The Lizalfos Chieftains are much larger and stronger variants of Lizalfos. They also appear in multiple main story Scenarios that include Volga, such as "[[The Sorceress of the Valley]]", "[[Land in the Sky]]", all Scenarios in Cia's Tale except "[[The Demon Lord]]", and even in a mission in ''[[Linkle's Tale]]'', "[[Powers Collide]]". Lizalfos Chieftains are portrayed as Volga's loyal servants, apologizing to their master when they must retreat during the battle with [[Ganondorf]] in the "Darkness Falls" Scenario. When defeated, Lizalfos may drop [[Lizalfos Scale]]s as bronze [[Material]]s and [[Lizalfos Gauntlet]]s as silver Materials. {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{CoH|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} Lizalfos appear as [[Enemy|Enemies]] in {{CoH}}. They are mostly stationary Enemies that move to the beat of the music, usually standing still while on the lookout for adventurers. Upon seeing one of the heroes, they will unsheathe their [[Sword]]s and proceed to charge at them, moving on every beat until they make contact with something. While charging, they can only move in one direction unless they step on a Bounce Trap, which will force them to turn and resume their chase elsewhere. Once contact has been made, they will be stunned for three beats, leaving them vulnerable to attack until they regain consciousness on the fourth beat. In the {{SotM}} [[Downloadable Content]] pack, they blend in with their surroundings until [[Skull Kid]] approaches them, similar to {{BotW|-}}. {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{AoC|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Stub|AoC}} Lizalfos are reptilian [[Monster]]s that can be encountered in [[Battle]]s all over [[Hyrule]] in eight varieties, first appearing in the [[Scenario]] "[[The Battle of Hyrule Field]]". They most often appear in large groups as foot soldiers, but can also be found as [[Powerful Foe]]s defending [[Enemy]]-controlled [[Outpost]]s. Some camouflage with their environment to ambush approaching [[Warrior]]s. Lizalfos drop [[Lizalfos Horn]]s, [[Lizalfos Tail|Tails]], and [[Lizalfos Talon|Talons]] when slain. After a [[Battle]] has been completed, the [[Warrior]]s will receive an amount of [[Lizalfos Trophy|Lizalfos Trophies]] equal to the amount of Lizalfos defeated during it. {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{AoI|-}}=== {{Checklist |game= AoI |type= Enemies |category= Enemies in Age of Imprisonment |needs= Detailed information on the following: * The Enemy's behavior * The Enemy's weaknesses }} {{Stub|AoI}} ==Trivia== *In {{TP|-}}, [[Missed Arrow]]s will stick to Lizalfos indefinitely and can be retrieved.{{Verify|TP}} ==Nomenclature== {{Nomenclature}} ==Gallery== {{All Images}} {{Gallery}} ==See Also== {{See Also| * Aeralfos * Dynalfos * Geru * Monster * Tokay }} {{Ref| {{Cite Book|quote= |book= E |publisher= |page= 190 {{Exp Game|OoT, OoT3D, TP, TPHD, SS}}}} {{Cite Guide|BotW Piggyback|page= 303|edition= Expanded Edition|year= 2018}} {{Cite|'''Lizalfos'''|Hyrule Compendium|BotW}} {{Cite|{{Big|Enhanced Lizal Spear}}
